pr_title: Add turn_on and turn_off to gree climate component
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Implements `async_turn_on` and `async_turn_off` which enable proper behaviour when calling climate.turn_on. Previously this would always reset the device to heat mode, now it will preserve the correct state of the device. **Gree** devices support power on/off command on the device interface.

issue_context.title: gree always default to heat mode
issue_context.body:
## The problem

switch to Cool mode, turn off device
turn on device using developer service request "climate.turn_on" (havcs component uses this request)

expected: Cool mode
actual: Heat mode

## Environment

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue:  0.117.5
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): None
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core):  x86_64, os_version | 5.4.69, python_version | 3.8.5
- Integration causing this issue: gree (same issue to all other climate components without turn_on implemented)
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/gree/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
None

## Traceback/Error logs
None

## Suggestion
gree component should implement async_turn_on and async_turn_off, since Pow (power) state is a separate state from Mod (mode) for gree AC devices


## Suggestion 2
also apply fix to climate component
in async_set_hvac_mode: remember non HVAC_MODE_OFF mode before setting to HVAC_MODE_OFF
in async_turn_on: use last remembered non-HVAC_MODE_OFF mode before trying HVAC_MODE_HEAT_COOL, HVAC_MODE_HEAT, HVAC_MODE_COOL

but this state won't persist across device reload
comments: Suggestion 1 makes sense, presuming this isn't an issue in the component requirements itself.

review_comments: Maybe this test should stay in place, this service was not removed, now was it ?

Sorry... deleted last response as I am trying to remember work I did here something like 2 months ago now.

This test is a power on test, the previous assertion wasn’t valid and introducing these service calls made that apparent. Since Gree uses two separate variables for mode  and power state, when sending power on the only reliable assertion is that it isn’t off.

In my previous implementation I didn’t really handle this well, so the test was carried out by setting a mode which implied the device would turn on (it was a bad way to test, IMHO). And in fact all it was really doing in the end was testing that a set mode was applied correctly, the test for modes is carried out further down, so this case still remains covered.
